topicName: High Availability Frameworks (InnoDB Cluster, MHA, Orchestrator)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"High Availability Frameworks in MySQL: InnoDB Cluster, MHA, and Orchestrator"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ensuring high availability (HA) for MySQL databases is critical for mission-critical applications. Without an HA strategy, a single server failure can lead to catastrophic downtime. This tutorial examines three of the most prominent HA solutions for MySQL: MySQL InnoDB Cluster, Master High Availability (MHA), and Orchestrator."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. MySQL InnoDB Cluster"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"MySQL InnoDB Cluster is the official, native high-availability solution provided by Oracle. It integrates MySQL Group Replication, MySQL Shell, and MySQL Router to deliver an out-of-the-box, easy-to-manage HA architecture without requiring third-party tools."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Group Replication: Provides built-in automatic failover and multi-master or single-master update capabilities."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"MySQL Shell: Offers advanced administrative capabilities, including JavaScript and Python APIs to configure and monitor the cluster."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"MySQL Router: Transparently routes client connections to the appropriate primary or secondary nodes in the cluster."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"// Example using MySQL Shell to create an InnoDB Cluster
var c = dba.createCluster('myCluster');
c.addInstance('user@mysql-node2:3306');
c.addInstance('user@mysql-node3:3306');"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Master High Availability (MHA for MySQL)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"MHA is a mature, open-source tool designed to handle asynchronous or semi-synchronous master failovers in a traditional MySQL replication topology. It monitors the master node and performs automated master failover rapidly, typically within 10 to 30 seconds."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Minimal downtime during master failure without complex multi-master setups."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Supports traditional asynchronous and semi-synchronous replication."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Identifies differing relay logs across slaves and applies them to the new master to prevent data loss."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"[server default]
manager_workdir=/var/log/mha
manager_log=/var/log/mha/mha.log
user=mha_admin
password=secret
repl_user=repl
repl_password=repl_secret

[server1]
host=192.168.1.10
role=master"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Orchestrator"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Orchestrator, developed by GitHub, is a powerful topology management and failover tool for MySQL replication. It supports both MySQL Group Replication and traditional asynchronous replication, providing a comprehensive web interface and CLI for visualization and automated recovery."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Provides real-time topological visualization and discovery of complex MySQL replication trees."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Supports both automated and manual master failover."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Offers an HTTP API for easy integration into existing orchestration and monitoring pipelines."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"{
  "DefaultHTTPAuthUser": "admin",
  "DefaultHTTPAuthPassword": "password",
  "MasterFailoverProcesses": [
    "/usr/local/bin/orc-hooks/master-failover.sh '{failureType}' '{failureDescription}' '{failedHost}' '{newMasterHost}'"
  ],
  "DiscoverByDBNameToClusterName": true
}"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Choosing the Right Framework"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Selecting the appropriate framework depends heavily on your database architecture and operational requirements. If you are starting fresh with MySQL 8.0, InnoDB Cluster is the recommended standard due to its native support and integrated routing. For existing legacy architectures using asynchronous replication, Orchestrator offers superior visualization and flexible failover controls, whereas MHA remains a lightweight choice for strict master-slave setups."}]
